question.text: A ball leaves the edge of a flat tabletop standing 4 m above the ground, rolling off horizontally with no initial drop. It touches down on the ground at a spot located 5 m away, measured horizontally from the table's edge. Determine how fast the ball was travelling the moment it left the tabletop.
conditions: ball rolls off the table edge horizontally (starts with zero vertical velocity)
table top is 4 m above the ground
landing point is 5 m horizontally from the table edge

figure.description: A right-angle layout: point A marks the table edge, point B is directly below A at the base of the table on the ground, 4 m below A. The ball leaves A moving horizontally (shown by an arrow v) and follows a curved path down to point C on the ground, which is 5 m horizontally from B.

solution.approach: Find the time of fall from the 4 m drop using g = 9.8 m/s² (no value given), then divide the 5 m horizontal distance by that time.

steps.text: Find the time to fall the 4 m height from rest, taking g = 9.8 m/s² since no value is given in the problem.
Divide the 5 m horizontal distance by this time to get the constant horizontal launch speed.

common_mistakes.text: Finding the time of fall as t = √(h/g) = √(4/9.8) ≈ 0.64 s, dropping the factor of 2 inside the square root, which gives a wrong speed of about 7.8 m/s.
